# Newspapers and periodicals (`newspapers_periodicals`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/communication.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Communication & information (`communication`)
- Deps: helped by printing_press, woodblock_printing, postal_system, free_press
- Core idea: A sheet printed at a regular interval (weekly, later daily) with dated reports from named places, sold by subscription and in the street and later paid for partly by advertisements. Regularity is what makes it work: readers come back, correspondents in many cities send reports by every post, and news becomes a commodity. Name the source and date of each report so readers can judge it. Regular issues depend on gathering and distributing news on time. Handwritten newsletters could circulate to subscribers; printing reached more readers.
- Pitfalls:
  - Calling Rome's Acta diurna or China's court gazettes the first newspapers: they were official bulletins, copied by hand or circulated to officials
  - Assuming press freedom: licensing, censorship and stamp taxes controlled papers almost everywhere until the 19th c.
  - Printing unverified rumour: early papers carried many false reports, and printed news spreads panic faster than talk
  - Expecting profit from sales alone: cheap papers lived from advertising
- History: rome: 59 BC – Caesar has daily public notices (acta diurna) posted, which were copied by hand and sent to the provinces; china: Tang and Song – court gazettes (dibao) circulated to officials, printed by the Song; Ming–Qing Peking Gazette (jingbao) printed and sold by commercial offices; europe: 16th c. – handwritten newsletters (avvisi) from Venice and Rome; 1605 Johann Carolus' Relation in Strasbourg, the first printed weekly; 1650 Leipzig Einkommende Zeitungen, the first daily; 1665 Oxford Gazette, renamed the London Gazette in 1666; 1702 Daily Courant; 1830s penny press; americas: 1690 – Publick Occurrences, Boston, suppressed after one issue; 1704 Boston News-Letter; india: 1780 – Hicky's Bengal Gazette, Calcutta; islamic: 1828 – al-Waqa'i' al-Misriyya, Cairo; 1831 Takvim-i Vekayi, Istanbul; east_asia: 1871 – Yokohama Mainichi, Japan's first Japanese-language daily; 1883 Hanseong sunbo in Korea
- Read:
  - Andrew Pettegree, The Invention of News: How the World Came to Know About Itself (2014)
  - Johannes Weber, Strassburg, 1605: The Origins of the Newspaper in Europe, German History 24 (2006)
